definition_zh: 鸟；禽类；（口语）人；飞行器
definition_en: an animal with feathers and wings, usually able to fly
core_image: 清晨的枝头，一只小鸟抖了抖羽毛开始鸣叫
scene: 清晨的花园里，一只小鸟落在篱笆上，抖了抖羽毛叫了两声。A small bird sat on the fence and sang.
sceneCN: 这里 bird 是「鸟」（第 1 个义项：有羽毛和翅膀的动物）；句意为一只小鸟落在篱笆上鸣叫。

pos.zh: 名词：鸟；禽类；（口语）人

derivatives.zh: 由 bird 加 -ie 构成，义为「小鸟」，也指羽毛球
由 bird 与 watcher 组合而成，义为「观鸟者」
由 bird 与 bath 组合而成，义为「供鸟戏水的浅水盆」

senses.title: The feathered animal
senses.definition: an animal with feathers, wings, and a beak, most kinds of which can fly
senses.definitionCN: 有羽毛、翅膀和喙的动物，大多数种类能飞
senses.example: A small bird sang in the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 一只小鸟在树上唱歌。
senses.why: Old English bridd first meant a nestling, and in Middle English the word widened until it named any feathered creature, which is now its main sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bridd 最初指雏鸟，到中古英语词义扩大，泛指任何有羽毛的动物，这就是今天的主要义项。

senses.title: Farm and game birds
senses.definition: birds kept for eggs, meat, or hunting, such as chickens and ducks
senses.definitionCN: 为取蛋、取肉或供狩猎而饲养的鸟，如鸡和鸭
senses.example: Farm birds need clean water every day.
senses.exampleCN: 家禽每天都需要干净的水。
senses.why: When the general word moved to wild birds, the older word fowl was left for farm and game birds, and bird took over part of that ground too.
senses.whyCN: 当通用词转向野生鸟类后，旧的 fowl 一词留给家禽与猎禽，而 bird 也接手了其中一部分用法。

senses.title: A person, in casual speech
senses.definition: used informally for a person, often one with odd or noticeable habits
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指某个人，常指习惯古怪或引人注意的人
senses.example: He is a strange bird.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个古怪的家伙。
senses.why: Comparing a person to a bird borrows the bird's quickness and odd habits, so the word became a light way to label someone.
senses.whyCN: 把人比作鸟，借用了鸟的轻快与古怪习性，于是这个词成了给人贴标签的轻松说法。

senses.title: An aircraft, in slang
senses.definition: used in informal speech for an aircraft, rocket, or spacecraft
senses.definitionCN: 非正式口语中指飞机、火箭或航天器
senses.example: The old bird still flies after forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这架老飞机飞了四十年还在飞。
senses.why: Both birds and aircraft fly, so pilots and engineers borrowed the word as a familiar name for a flying machine.
senses.whyCN: 鸟和飞行器都会飞，于是飞行员与工程师借这个词来亲切地称呼飞行器。

intro.en: Bird is an old English word that began as the name of a nestling and later replaced the general word for bird.
intro.cn: bird 是古老的英语词，最初指雏鸟，后来取代了表示「鸟」的通用词。

items.en: Old English bridd meant a young bird or nestling, while the general word for a bird was fugol.
items.cn: 古英语 bridd 指雏鸟，而当时表示「鸟」的通用词是 fugol。

items.en: In Middle English bird spread from the nestling to any bird, and fugol fell out of use.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，bird 从雏鸟扩展到任何鸟，而 fugol 逐渐退出使用。

items.en: The older fowl was pushed back to mean farm birds and their meat, leaving bird as the general term.
items.cn: 更早的 fowl 被收窄为家禽及其肉，bird 则成为通用说法。

items.en: In modern slang the same word also names a person and an aircraft, because both are noticed for movement and flight.
items.cn: 在现代俚语里，这个词也指人和飞行器，因为两者都以活动和飞行引人注意。

items.en: Today bird means any feathered animal and appears in many fixed phrases such as early bird.
items.cn: 今天 bird 指任何有羽毛的动物，并出现在 early bird 等许多固定说法里。

note.cn: 形近组收读音相近的短词；近义组收其他表示鸟类的名称。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小鸟」，也指羽毛球。

entries.definition: The hair growing on a man's chin and cheeks.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胡须」，拼写与 bird 相近。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「禽类」，尤指家禽或猎禽。

entries.definition: Farm birds kept for eggs and meat, considered as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「家禽」，作为整体指为蛋和肉饲养的鸟。

entries.definition: A small brown bird common in towns and gardens.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「麻雀」，一种常见于城镇花园的小褐鸟。

entries.definition: A soft-voiced bird often used as a symbol of peace.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鸽子」，叫声柔和，常作和平的象征。

normal.en: Old English bridd meant a nestling, and Middle English let the word cover every bird.

normal.en: Bird replaced the older word fugol, which is why bird is the everyday term today.
normal.cn: bird 取代了更早的 fugol，所以今天日常说的就是 bird。

normal.en: A bird and an aircraft both fly, which is how the slang sense grew.
normal.cn: 鸟和飞行器都会飞，俚语义就是这样长出来的。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with nest, watching, early and flu.
normal.cn: 它常与 nest、watching、early、flu 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-i-r-d; the letters ir make the vowel sound in the middle.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-i-r-d，中间的 ir 发出这个词的元音。

abstract.en: See a small bird on a fence at dawn, feathers fluffed and throat moving: that is bird.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时篱笆上的一只小鸟，羽毛蓬起、喉部起伏，那就是 bird。

abstract.en: Give the same picture wings of metal and it becomes the slang for an aircraft.
abstract.cn: 给同一幅画换上金属翅膀，它就成了指飞行器的俚语。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the fence and the feathers bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让篱笆与羽毛把意思带回来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伯德」——伯伯养的那只鸟最会叫：鸟

root: bird 来自古英语 bridd，最初只指雏鸟，当时表示「鸟」的通用词是 fugol。中古英语里 bird 的词义扩大为任何鸟，fugol 退场，fowl 则被收窄为家禽与禽肉。现代俚语又把会飞的特点借给了人和飞行器。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bird rest on one picture: a feathered creature that flies, and then anything else that borrows its flight or its quickness.
sensesIntro.cn: bird 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：一只有羽毛、会飞的动物，随后凡是借用它的飞行或轻快特点的事物也跟着叫这个名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bird on a fence at dawn
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明时篱笆上的一只小鸟

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: feathers and wings make the everyday sense of any bird.
branches.cn: 动物线：羽毛与翅膀构成「鸟」这个日常义项。

branches.en: THE FARM: birds kept for eggs, meat and hunting keep the older fowl ground.
branches.cn: 饲养线：为蛋、肉与狩猎而养的鸟保留了旧词 fowl 的地盘。

branches.en: THE PERSON: quickness and odd habits let the word name a human being.
branches.cn: 人物线：轻快与古怪习性让这个词可以用来指人。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: anything that flies can borrow the name in slang.
branches.cn: 机器线：任何会飞的东西都能在俚语里借走这个名字。

branches.en: THE FLIGHT: one shared ability links the animal and the aircraft.
branches.cn: 飞行线：同一种能力把动物与飞行器连在一起。

definition_zh: 出生；分娩；诞生；出身
definition_en: the time when a baby comes out of its mother's body, or the beginning of something
core_image: 产房门口的一只小摇篮，旁边放着写有日期的卡片
scene: 医院的走廊上，父亲在登记表上填下孩子出生的日期。She recorded the date of her son's birth.
sceneCN: 这里 birth 是「出生」（第 1 个义项：婴儿降生这一事实）；句意为她记下了儿子出生的日期。

pos.zh: 名词：出生；分娩；诞生；出身

derivatives.zh: 由 birth 与 day 组合而成，义为「生日」
由 birth 与 place 组合而成，义为「出生地」
由 birth 与 rate 组合而成，义为「出生率」

senses.title: The arrival of a baby
senses.definition: the event in which a baby is born and begins life outside the mother
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿降生、开始在母体外生活这一事件
senses.example: She recorded the date of her son's birth.
senses.exampleCN: 她记下了儿子出生的日期。
senses.why: Old English gebyrd came from the verb beran, to bear or carry, so birth names the moment a child is brought into the world.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gebyrd 来自动词 beran「承载、生育」，所以 birth 指的是孩子被带到世上的那一刻。

senses.title: The act of giving birth
senses.definition: the process by which a woman or an animal gives birth
senses.definitionCN: 女性或动物生下幼崽的过程
senses.example: The birth was long but safe.
senses.exampleCN: 分娩过程很长，但很顺利。
senses.why: Because the same noun covers both the event and the effort behind it, birth can also name the whole process of delivery.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既覆盖事件本身，也覆盖其后的努力，所以 birth 也可以指整个分娩过程。

senses.title: The beginning of something
senses.definition: the time when an idea, an organization, or a country begins
senses.definitionCN: 某个想法、组织或国家开始出现的时间
senses.example: The birth of the internet changed daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网的诞生改变了日常生活。
senses.why: A new idea arrives the way a baby does, suddenly and with a date, so the word for human arrival was borrowed for the start of anything.
senses.whyCN: 新想法到来时就像婴儿降生，有突然性也有日期，于是表示人降生的词被借去指任何事物的开始。

senses.title: Family origin
senses.definition: the social rank or family that a person comes from
senses.definitionCN: 一个人来自的社会等级或家族
senses.example: He is of noble birth.
senses.exampleCN: 他出身贵族。
senses.why: Since family line is fixed at the moment of birth, the word for that moment also came to mean the rank one is born into.
senses.whyCN: 家世在出生的那一刻就定下了，所以表示那一刻的词也引申为「生来所属的等级」。

intro.en: Birth began as a prefixed noun from the verb bear, and the prefix later dropped away.
intro.cn: birth 最初是由动词 bear 加前缀构成的名词，前缀后来脱落了。

items.en: Old English gebyrd came from beran, meaning to bear or to give birth.
items.cn: 古英语 gebyrd 来自 beran，意为「承载、生育」。

items.en: The same verb survives in bear a child and in the related noun burden.
items.cn: 同一个动词仍见于 bear a child，也见于相关名词 burden。

items.en: The old prefix dropped away and the plain form birth became the standard noun.
items.cn: 旧前缀脱落，朴素的 birth 成为标准名词。

items.en: From a person's arrival the word spread to the start of ideas, nations, and organizations.
items.cn: 从人的降生出发，这个词扩展到思想、国家与组织的开端。

items.en: Because family rank is fixed at birth, the word also came to mean social origin.
items.cn: 因为家族等级在出生时就定了，这个词也引申为「社会出身」。

items.en: Today birth covers delivery, origin, and the founding moment of almost anything.
items.cn: 今天 birth 可指分娩、出身，以及几乎任何事物的创立时刻。

note.cn: 形近组收读音几乎相同的词；近义组收表示「分娩、起源」的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to carry or to give birth.

normal.en: Birth comes from bear: to give birth is to bear a child, and the prefix later fell away.

normal.en: Birth, birthday, birthplace and birthrate all keep the same first element.

normal.en: A new country or a new idea also has a birth, because both arrive with a date.
normal.cn: 新国家或新想法也有 birth，因为两者都带着一个日期到来。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with give, date of, certificate and rate.
normal.cn: 它常与 give、date of、certificate、rate 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-i-r-t-h; the th at the end is the same ending as in fourth.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-i-r-t-h，末尾的 th 与 fourth 的结尾相同。

abstract.cn: 想象产房外的一只小摇篮，旁边放着写有日期的卡片，那就是 birth。

abstract.en: Put a light bulb in the cradle instead of a baby and the word becomes the start of an idea.
abstract.cn: 把摇篮里的婴儿换成一个灯泡，这个词就变成「想法的开端」。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the cradle bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让摇篮把意思带回来。

examples.cn: 互联网的诞生改变了日常生活。

examples.en: He is of noble birth.
examples.cn: 他出身贵族。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of birth come from one moment: a new life arriving, and everything fixed or begun at that moment.
sensesIntro.cn: birth 的四个义项都出自同一个时刻：新生命到来，以及在这一刻被定下或开启的一切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cradle outside a hospital room with a date card
core.cn: 核心意象：产房外的一只摇篮和一张写有日期的卡片

branches.en: THE ARRIVAL: the first sense is the baby coming into the world.
branches.cn: 降生线：第一个义项就是婴儿来到世上。

branches.en: THE EFFORT: the same noun covers the delivery that makes the arrival happen.
branches.cn: 分娩线：同一个名词也覆盖促成降生的分娩过程。

branches.en: THE START: ideas and nations arrive with a date, so they also have a birth.
branches.cn: 开端线：思想与国家也带着日期到来，所以它们也有 birth。

branches.en: THE RANK: the family one is born into fixes one's social origin.
branches.cn: 等级线：出生的家族决定了一个人的社会出身。

branches.cn: 同一形状：婴儿与新想法都在某个被标记的时刻开始。

definition_zh: 生日；诞辰；生日聚会
definition_en: the day each year when a person was born, or the celebration held on that day
core_image: 插着蜡烛的蛋糕，桌上散着彩纸和礼物
scene: 晚饭后，家人关掉灯，把插着蜡烛的蛋糕端上桌。My birthday is in June.
sceneCN: 这里 birthday 是「生日」（第 1 个义项：每年出生的那个日子）；句意为我的生日在六月。

pos.zh: 名词：生日；诞辰；生日聚会

derivatives.zh: 由 birth 与 date 组合而成，义为「出生日期」
口语说法，字面为「生日礼服」，实指赤裸的身体

senses.title: The yearly date of birth
senses.definition: the day of the year on which a person was born, remembered each year
senses.definitionCN: 一年中某人出生的那个日子，每年都会纪念
senses.example: My birthday is in June.
senses.exampleCN: 我的生日在六月。
senses.why: The word simply joins birth with day, so it first names the calendar date on which someone was born.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只是把 birth 与 day 合在一起，所以它首先指某人出生在日历上的那一天。

senses.title: The celebration
senses.definition: a party or celebration held to mark a birthday
senses.definitionCN: 为庆祝生日而举办的聚会或庆祝活动
senses.example: We are going to a birthday on Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 周六我们要去参加一个生日聚会。
senses.why: In casual speech the day and the party held on it share one word, so going to a birthday means going to the celebration.
senses.whyCN: 在口语里，这一天和为它办的聚会被同一个词覆盖，所以说去一个 birthday 就是去参加庆祝会。

senses.title: The founding date of a group
senses.definition: the yearly date on which an important person or organization was founded
senses.definitionCN: 重要人物或机构每年被纪念的诞生或成立之日
senses.example: The school celebrated its hundredth birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校庆祝了它的百岁诞辰。
senses.why: Schools and nations are pictured as living things that were born on a date, so birthday also marks their founding anniversary.
senses.whyCN: 学校与国家被当作在某天诞生的生命体，所以 birthday 也用来标记它们的成立纪念日。

intro.en: Birthday is a plain English compound of birth and day, and its party sense is much newer.
intro.cn: birthday 是 birth 与 day 组成的朴素英语复合词，而「聚会」义要晚得多。

items.en: Old English byrddaeg joined gebyrd, birth, with daeg, day.
items.cn: 古英语 byrddaeg 把 gebyrd「出生」与 daeg「日子」合在一起。

items.en: The compound survived with the shortened first element birth, matching the noun birth.
items.cn: 这一复合词保留下来，第一个成分缩短为 birth，与名词 birth 一致。

items.en: Birthday cakes and candles spread in the nineteenth century and made the day a family occasion.
items.cn: 生日蛋糕与蜡烛在十九世纪流行开来，使这一天成为家庭节日。

items.en: In modern speech a birthday can also name the party held on that day, as in going to a birthday.
items.cn: 现代口语里，birthday 也可指当天举办的聚会，如 go to a birthday。

items.en: The word spread to the founding day of schools, cities, and nations.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到了学校、城市与国家的成立纪念日。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the two parts and similar day words; the near-meaning group collects ceremony and calendar words.
note.cn: 形近组收两个构件与相近的 day 词；近义组收仪式与日期用词。

entries.definition: The noun for being born, the first half of birthday.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出生」，是 birthday 的前半部分。

entries.definition: The exact date on which a person was born.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出生日期」。

entries.definition: A day free from work or a special day of rest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「假日、节日」，词尾与 birthday 相同。

entries.definition: A period of twenty-four hours.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一天」，是 birthday 的后半部分。

entries.definition: A date remembered each year because of an event in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「周年纪念日」，指每年纪念的往日事件。

entries.definition: Relating to birth, as in natal day.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「出生的」，如 natal day 出生之日。

entries.definition: A party or event held to mark a happy occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「庆祝活动」。

entries.definition: A particular day of a month or year.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「日期」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded compound, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的复合方式、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Birth plus day is exactly what the word means: the day of one's birth.
normal.cn: birth 加 day 正是这个词的意思：出生的那一天。

normal.en: Old English already had byrddaeg, so this compound is very old.
normal.cn: 古英语里已有 byrddaeg，可见这个复合词非常古老。

normal.en: Cakes and candles made the day a family party, which is why birthday can mean the celebration.
normal.cn: 蛋糕与蜡烛让这一天成了家庭聚会，所以 birthday 也能指那场庆祝。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with happy, party, card, cake and present.
normal.cn: 它常与 happy、party、card、cake、present 搭配。

normal.en: Spell birthday as one word: birth then day, with no space.
normal.cn: 拼写是连写的 birthday：先 birth 后 day，中间不留空格。

abstract.en: See a cake with candles and coloured paper on the table: that is birthday.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上一个插着蜡烛的蛋糕和散落的彩纸，那就是 birthday。

abstract.en: Move the cake to a school hall and the same word becomes a founding anniversary.
abstract.cn: 把蛋糕挪到学校礼堂，同一个词就变成「成立纪念日」。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the candles bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让蜡烛把意思带回来。

examples.en: My birthday is in June.
examples.cn: 我的生日在六月。

examples.en: We are going to a birthday on Saturday.
examples.cn: 周六我们要去参加一个生日聚会。

examples.en: The school celebrated its hundredth birthday.
examples.cn: 这所学校庆祝了它的百岁诞辰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必是得」——过生日必是得许个愿：生日

root: birthday 由 birth 与 day 直接合成，古英语已有 byrddaeg 这样的形式。它首先指每年出生的那个日子；十九世纪生日蛋糕与蜡烛流行后，这一天成了家庭节日，口语里 birthday 又可指当天的聚会；学校、城市与国家也被当作有生日的生命体，于是又指成立纪念日。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of birthday all mark one date: the day of a birth, the party on that day, and the founding day of a group.
sensesIntro.cn: birthday 的三个义项都标记同一个日子：出生的那天、当天的聚会，以及团体的成立之日。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cake with candles and coloured paper on a table
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上插着蜡烛的蛋糕与彩纸

branches.en: THE DATE: the plainest sense is the day of the year one was born.
branches.cn: 日期线：最朴素的义项就是一年中出生的那一天。

branches.en: THE PARTY: the cake and candles turn the date into a celebration.
branches.cn: 聚会线：蛋糕与蜡烛把这个日子变成庆祝活动。

branches.en: THE GROUP: a school or nation also has a founding day to mark.
branches.cn: 团体线：学校或国家也有值得纪念的成立之日。

branches.en: THE DAY: the date and the party share one word in everyday speech.
branches.cn: 同一天：日期与聚会在口语里共用同一个词。

branches.en: THE EXTENSION: treating a group as a living thing gives it a birthday.
branches.cn: 延伸线：把团体当作生命体，它就拥有了生日。

intro.en: Birthday is a transparent compound; the items below are its two parts and the words built on them.
intro.cn: birthday 是结构透明的复合词，下面列出的是它的两个构件以及建立在这些成分上的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin phrase dies natalis means birthday, and natalis is listed as a parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语短语 dies natalis 意为「生日」，其中 natalis 作为平行词列出。

items.example: It is the first part of birthday.

items.example: It is the second part of birthday.

items.example: Her birthday falls on a Sunday.
items.exampleCN: 她的生日正好是星期天。

definition_zh: 饼干；小点心；浅褐色
definition_en: a small flat baked cake, crisp in British use and soft in American use
core_image: 一盘刚出炉的脆饼，边缘微微焦黄
scene: 下午茶时间，奶奶把一块脆饼掰成两半，放进茶杯里蘸了蘸。She dunked a biscuit in her tea.
sceneCN: 这里 biscuit 是「饼干」（第 1 个义项：英式脆饼）；句意为她把一块饼干蘸进茶里。

pos.zh: 名词：饼干；小点心；浅褐色

derivatives.zh: 由 biscuit 加 -y 构成，义为「饼干般的；饼干味的」
同源借词，来自意大利语，义为「意大利脆饼」

senses.title: The crisp baked cake
senses.definition: a small flat cake baked until crisp, eaten with tea or as a snack
senses.definitionCN: 一种小而扁的糕点，烤至酥脆，配茶或作零食食用
senses.example: She dunked a biscuit in her tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一块饼干蘸进茶里。
senses.why: Latin bis coctus means twice cooked, and the crisp British biscuit is exactly bread baked twice to drive the moisture out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 bis coctus 意为「烤两次」，而英式脆饼正是经过两次烘烤、把水分逼干的饼。

senses.title: A soft quick bread
senses.definition: in American English, a small soft bread similar to a scone, often eaten with gravy
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语中指类似司康的小型软面包，常配肉汁吃
senses.example: She baked biscuits for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她烤了小软饼当早饭。
senses.why: American cooks used the borrowed word for a soft quick bread, so the same spelling names two quite different baked goods.
senses.whyCN: 美国厨师用这个借来的词来指一种软质的快手面包，于是同一个拼写指两种颇为不同的烘焙食品。

senses.title: A pale brown colour
senses.definition: a pale warm brown colour like a baked biscuit
senses.definitionCN: 像烤好的饼干那样浅而暖的褐色
senses.example: The walls were painted biscuit.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成了浅褐色。
senses.why: Food words often become colour words, and the warm baked tone of a biscuit gave this paint and fabric shade its name.
senses.whyCN: 食物名称常常变成颜色名称，饼干那种温暖的烘焙色就给了这种涂料与布料色调一个名字。

intro.en: Biscuit is a Latin phrase that travelled through French and split into two national meanings in English.
intro.cn: biscuit 是一个经法语传入英语的拉丁语短语，在英语里分成了两种国别用法。

items.en: Latin bis coctus meant twice cooked, describing bread baked twice so that it would keep.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bis coctus 意为「烤两次」，描述为便于保存而烘烤两遍的面包。

items.en: Old French bescuit carried the same twice-baked idea across the Channel.
items.cn: 古法语 bescuit 把同一个「烤两次」的意思带过了海峡。

items.en: Early English spellings varied, and the form biscuit eventually settled.
items.cn: 早期英语拼写有多种，最终固定为 biscuit。

items.en: British English kept the crisp meaning, while American English applied the word to a soft quick bread.
items.cn: 英式英语保留「脆」的意思，美式英语则把这个词用于一种软质的快手面包。

items.en: The pale baked colour of a biscuit gave the word a third sense for paint and cloth.
items.cn: 饼干那种浅淡的烘焙色，给这个词添了第三个义项，用于涂料与布料。

items.en: Today biscuit is a snack word in Britain and a breakfast bread word in America.
items.cn: 今天 biscuit 在英国是零食词，在美国则是早餐面食词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the same-origin Italian word and similar sounds; the near-meaning group collects other baked snacks.
note.cn: 形近组收同源的意大利语词与读音相近的词；近义组收其他烘焙点心。

entries.definition: Italian crisp biscuits, baked twice like the original Latin name says.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「意大利脆饼」，与拉丁语原名一样经过两次烘烤。

entries.definition: To cut something into two equal parts.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「平分、对切」，与 biscuit 共享表示「二」的前缀。

entries.definition: A container made of woven material.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「篮子」，读音与 biscuit 相近。

entries.definition: A small sweet cake, the usual American word for a biscuit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「曲奇饼干」，是美式英语里对饼干的常用说法。

entries.definition: A thin dry biscuit that snaps when broken.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薄脆饼」，掰开时会发出脆响。

entries.definition: A small round cake of flour and fat, often eaten with tea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「司康饼」，一种面粉与油脂做的小圆饼，常配茶。

entries.definition: A very thin crisp biscuit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「威化薄饼」，一种极薄的脆饼。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的拉丁短语、真实同源词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Bis means twice and coctus means cooked, so a biscuit is bread cooked twice.

normal.en: Italian biscotti keeps the same Latin idea and the same crisp texture.
normal.cn: 意大利语 biscotti 保留了同样的拉丁观念和同样的脆质地。

normal.en: Britain eats crisp biscuits with tea, while America bakes soft biscuits for breakfast.
normal.cn: 英国人配茶吃脆饼干，美国人则把软饼当早餐。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with tin, crumbs, chocolate and tea.
normal.cn: 它常与 tin、crumbs、chocolate、tea 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-i-s-c-u-i-t: the ui pair sits in the middle and is easy to drop.

abstract.en: See a tray of pale golden rounds just out of the oven: that is biscuit.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘刚出炉的浅金色圆饼，那就是 biscuit。

abstract.en: Soften the same round into a breakfast bread and the word changes nationality.
abstract.cn: 把同一个圆饼变软成早餐面包，这个词就换了国别用法。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the warm tray bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那盘温热的饼把意思带回来。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of biscuit all start at the same oven: a twice-baked cake, the soft American version, and the warm colour it takes on.
sensesIntro.cn: biscuit 的三个义项都从同一个烤炉出发：烤两次的饼、美式软饼，以及它烤出来的暖色调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tray of pale golden rounds fresh from the oven
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘刚出炉的浅金色圆饼

branches.en: THE CRISP ONE: twice-baked bread is the British biscuit dipped in tea.
branches.cn: 脆饼线：烤两次的面包就是配茶吃的英式饼干。

branches.en: THE SOFT ONE: American cooks applied the same word to a quick soft bread.
branches.cn: 软饼线：美国厨师把同一个词用在了软质快手面包上。

branches.en: THE COLOUR: the baked tone of the crust became a paint and cloth shade.
branches.cn: 颜色线：饼皮的烘焙色成了涂料与布料的色调。

branches.en: THE SAME CRUST: what you eat and what you see share one warm surface.
branches.cn: 同一层皮：你吃的东西与你看到的颜色共用一层暖色表面。

branches.en: THE TWO TONGUES: one borrowed word grew two different foods in two countries.
branches.cn: 两种语言线：一个借词在两个国家长成两种不同的食品。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bis 与 coctus 是这个词背后两个有记录的成分。

items.exampleCN: 它是 biscuit 背后那个拉丁短语的第一个成分。

definition_zh: 一点；小块；一会儿；（计算机）比特
definition_en: a small piece or amount of something, a short time, or the smallest unit of data in computing
core_image: 从一整块面包上掰下来的一小角
scene: 餐桌上，孩子从整块面包上掰下一小块递给妹妹。He tore off a bit of bread and gave it to her.
sceneCN: 这里 bit 是「一点；小块」（第 1 个义项：从整体上分出的一小部分）；句意为他掰下一小块面包递给她。

pos.zh: 名词：一点；小块；一会儿；比特
动词：bite 的过去式，义为「咬」

derivatives.zh: 由 bit 加 -y 构成，义为「零碎的；琐碎的」
由 bit 与 -wise 构成，义为「逐位地」，用于计算机领域

senses.title: A small piece
senses.definition: a small piece cut or broken off from something larger
senses.definitionCN: 从较大的东西上切下或掰下的一小块
senses.example: He gave me a bit of his chocolate.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了我一点他的巧克力。
senses.why: Old English bita meant the piece bitten off, so the first sense is a fragment taken from something bigger.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bita 指被咬下来的一块，所以第一个义项就是从较大物体上取下的一小份。

senses.title: A small amount
senses.definition: a small amount of a substance or of a quality
senses.definitionCN: 少量物质，或某种性质的一点点
senses.example: Add a bit of salt to the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 往汤里加一点盐。
senses.why: The same piece image is used for an amount you cannot count, such as salt or patience.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅「小块」的画面被用在数不清的少量事物上，比如盐或耐心。

senses.title: A short time
senses.definition: a short period of time
senses.definitionCN: 很短的一段时间
senses.example: Wait a bit before you open the door.
senses.exampleCN: 等一会儿再开门。
senses.why: A small piece of time is still a piece: the word cuts a short slice out of the day.
senses.whyCN: 一小段时间同样是一小份：这个词从一天里切出短短的一截。

senses.title: The binary unit
senses.definition: the smallest unit of information in a computer, either zero or one
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中最小的信息单位，取值只能是零或一
senses.example: One bit can hold only zero or one.
senses.exampleCN: 一个比特只能存零或一。
senses.why: Computer science took the word for a small piece and made it the smallest possible piece of data.
senses.whyCN: 计算机科学借用了「一小块」这个词，把它变成数据里最小的一块。

intro.en: Bit began as the name of a piece bitten off, and the same short word later covered time, amount and computer data.
intro.cn: bit 最初指被咬下来的一块，这个短词后来覆盖了时间、数量与计算机数据。

items.en: Old English bita meant a piece bitten off, and it came from the verb bitan, to bite.
items.cn: 古英语 bita 指被咬下来的一块，源自动词 bitan，意思是「咬」。

items.en: The verb bitan became modern bite, so the noun and the verb started life as one family.
items.cn: 动词 bitan 变成今天的 bite，所以这个名词和动词原本同出一族。

items.en: The noun kept the short form bit and spread from food to any small piece.
items.cn: 这个名词保留了短形式 bit，并从食物扩展到任何小块。

items.en: Later the same word was used for a short time and for a small amount of anything.
items.cn: 后来这个词也被用来指一小段时间和任何事物的少量。

items.en: In the twentieth century computing gave bit a technical sense: the smallest unit of data.
items.cn: 二十世纪的计算机领域给 bit 一个技术义：最小的数据单位。

normal.en: Old English bita was the piece bitten off, so bit begins as a fragment of food.

normal.cn: 一点时间和一点盐用的是同一幅画面：切下来的一小份。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with of, by, quite and pieces.

abstract.en: See a hand tearing one corner off a loaf: that corner is a bit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从整条面包上撕下一角：那一角就是 bit。

abstract.en: Shrink that corner until it is only a moment or a single zero, and the word still fits.
abstract.cn: 把那一角缩小到只剩片刻，或缩成一个零，这个词仍然适用。

abstract.en: Say bit, then let the torn corner bring back the small piece.
abstract.cn: 先读 bit，再让撕下的那一角把「小块」的意思带回来。

examples.en: He gave me a bit of his chocolate.
examples.cn: 他给了我一点他的巧克力。

examples.en: Wait a bit before you open the door.
examples.cn: 等一会儿再开门。

examples.en: One bit can hold only zero or one.
examples.cn: 一个比特只能存零或一。

root: bit 来自古英语 bita，意思是「咬下来的一块」，源自动词 bitan（咬），这个词也给出今天的 bite。名词从中古英语的短形式 bit 一路保留，先指食物的一小块，后扩展到少量与片刻，二十世纪又成为计算机里最小的数据单位。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bit rest on one picture: a small piece taken off something larger.
sensesIntro.cn: bit 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：从更大物体上取下的一小块。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner torn off a loaf of bread
core.cn: 核心意象：从整条面包上撕下的一角

branches.en: THE PIECE: a fragment cut or torn from something larger keeps the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 小块线：从较大物体上切下或撕下的一点，保留最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE AMOUNT: salt and patience are measured with the same small piece.
branches.cn: 数量线：盐和耐心都用同一「一小块」来计量。

branches.en: THE MOMENT: a short slice of time is a small piece of the day.
branches.cn: 时间线：一天里切出的短短一截，就是一小份时间。

branches.en: THE DATA: computing turned the small piece into the smallest unit of information.
branches.cn: 数据线：计算机把这一小块变成最小的信息单位。

branches.en: THE FRAGMENT: a countable piece and an uncountable amount share one image.
branches.cn: 碎块线：可数的一小块与不可数的少量共享同一幅画面。

definition_en: of the darkest colour, without light, or (of coffee) served without milk
core_image: 停电的深夜，屋里没有一丝光
scene: 停电的晚上，屋里一片漆黑，他摸黑找到了手电筒。The room was black until he found a torch.
sceneCN: 这里 black 是「黑暗的」（第 2 个义项：没有光线的）；句意为屋里一片漆黑，直到他找到手电。

senses.title: The darkest colour
senses.definition: of the darkest colour, like ink, coal or the night sky
senses.definitionCN: 颜色最深的，像墨、煤或夜空那样
senses.example: She wore a black coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一件黑色大衣。
senses.why: Old English blæc named the colour of soot and burnt wood, and that is still the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 blæc 指烟灰和被烧过的木头那种颜色，这仍然是它最核心的义项。

senses.title: Without light
senses.definition: with no light at all, so that nothing can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 完全没有光线，什么也看不见
senses.example: The street was black after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，街上漆黑一片。
senses.why: A place with no light looks like the colour black, so the same word covers darkness.
senses.whyCN: 没有光的地方看上去就是黑色，所以同一个词也覆盖了「黑暗」。

senses.title: Coffee without milk
senses.definition: served without milk or cream, used of coffee
senses.definitionCN: 不加牛奶或奶油的，用于咖啡
senses.example: He drinks black coffee every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上都喝不加奶的咖啡。
senses.why: Coffee without milk looks black in the cup, so the colour word became a way to order it.
senses.whyCN: 不加奶的咖啡在杯子里看上去是黑的，于是这个颜色词成了点单时的说法。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: used, usually with a capital letter, for people of African origin or descent
senses.definitionCN: 通常大写，指非洲裔或具有非洲血统的人群
senses.example: Black writers have shaped modern literature.
senses.exampleCN: 黑人作家塑造了现代文学。
senses.why: The colour word was long used as a label for people of African descent; today the capitalised form is the usual self-chosen term.
senses.whyCN: 这个词长期被用作非洲裔人群的称谓；今天大写的 Black 是他们常用的自我称谓。

intro.en: Black is an old English colour word, and it has grown from soot and darkness to coffee, clothing and people.
intro.cn: black 是古老的英语颜色词，从烟灰与黑暗一路扩展到咖啡、衣着与人群。

items.en: Old English blæc meant black or dark, and it was used of soot, pitch and burnt wood.
items.cn: 古英语 blæc 表示黑或暗，用于烟灰、沥青和被烧过的木头。

items.en: The word is related to a Germanic root for burning, because burnt things turn black.
items.cn: 这个词与日耳曼语中表示「燃烧」的词根相关，因为烧过的东西会变黑。

items.en: Old English also had blac, meaning pale, a look-alike that later disappeared.
items.cn: 古英语里还有 blac，意思是「苍白」，这个形近词后来消失了。

items.en: The colour word spread to darkness, mourning clothes and bad luck.
items.cn: 这个颜色词扩展到黑暗、丧服与坏运气。

items.en: Today black also describes coffee without milk and, capitalised, a group of people.
items.cn: 今天 black 也形容不加奶的咖啡，大写时还指一个族群。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「空白的」，拼写与 black 相近。

entries.definition: Cold, empty and without hope.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒凉的；无望的」，拼写与 black 相近。

entries.definition: With little or no light.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「暗的」，指光线很少或没有。

entries.definition: Not bright, but still able to be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「昏暗的」，指不亮但仍能看见。

entries.definition: A very hard black wood, often used for the colour itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「乌木；乌黑色」，常用作黑色的代称。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with coffee, market, board and out.

abstract.en: See a room with no lamp, only the dark: that darkness is black.
abstract.cn: 想象一间没有灯的房间，只有黑暗：那种黑就是 black。

abstract.en: Pour coffee without milk and the cup shows the same colour.
abstract.cn: 倒入不加奶的咖啡，杯子里呈现的是同一种颜色。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the unlit room bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那间没有灯的房间把意思带回来。

sensesIntro.cn: black 的四个义项都从同一个画面上长出来：烟灰的颜色，以及一切与这种黑暗相通的事物。

core.cn: 核心意象：夜里没有开灯的屋子，一丝光也没有

branches.en: THE COLOUR: soot, ink and coal give the oldest sense of black.
branches.cn: 颜色线：烟灰、墨与煤给出 black 最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE DARK: a place without light looks like the colour itself.
branches.cn: 黑暗线：没有光的地方看上去就是这种颜色本身。

branches.cn: 色调线：颜色与「没有光」共享同一幅核心画面。

definition_zh: 失明的；瞎的；盲目的；盲人；百叶窗；使失明
definition_en: unable to see, done without thought or reason, or to make someone unable to see
core_image: 一根白色手杖在墙边轻轻探路
scene: 一位盲人拄着白色手杖，沿着墙边慢慢向前走。The blind man walked slowly along the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 blind 是「失明的」（第 1 个义项：看不见东西的）；句意为那位盲人沿着墙慢慢走。

pos.zh: 形容词：失明的；盲目的
名词：盲人（与 the 连用）；百叶窗
动词：使失明；使看不见

collocations.zh: 相亲；由他人安排的约会

derivatives.zh: 由 blind 加 -ness 构成，义为「失明；盲目」

senses.title: Unable to see
senses.definition: not able to see, either from birth or because of illness or injury
senses.definitionCN: 看不见东西的，可能是天生，也可能因疾病或受伤
senses.example: The blind woman used a white cane.
senses.exampleCN: 那位失明的女士用一根白色手杖。
senses.why: Old English blind already meant unable to see, and that physical sense has never left the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 blind 已经表示看不见，这个身体层面的义项从未离开这个词。

senses.title: Without judgement
senses.definition: done or felt without thinking clearly or judging fairly
senses.definitionCN: 未经清醒思考或公正判断就做出的、产生的
senses.example: Love can make people blind to faults.
senses.exampleCN: 爱会让人对缺点视而不见。
senses.why: A person who cannot see becomes a picture of someone who will not judge clearly, so the word moved from eyes to mind.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的人变成了不肯看清的人的比喻，于是这个词从眼睛移到心智。

senses.title: People who cannot see
senses.definition: used with the definite article to mean people who cannot see, as a group
senses.definitionCN: 与定冠词连用，作为一个群体指看不见的人
senses.example: The charity helps the blind.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构帮助盲人。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a group noun with the, and blind follows that old pattern.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用 the 把形容词变成群体名词，blind 遵循的就是这个古老的模式。

senses.title: The window covering
senses.definition: a window covering made of slats that can be pulled down or tilted
senses.definitionCN: 由可放下或倾斜的板条制成的窗饰
senses.example: She closed the blinds before the sun rose.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳升起前她拉上了百叶窗。
senses.why: The covering shuts light out the way blindness shuts sight out, so the same word was given to it.
senses.whyCN: 这种窗饰把光挡在外面，正如失明把视线挡在外面，于是它得到同一个名字。

senses.title: To make unable to see
senses.definition: to make someone unable to see, often suddenly and temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 使人看不见，常指突然而短暂的
senses.example: The bright flash blinded him for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 那道强光让他一瞬间看不见了。
senses.why: The adjective became a verb: to put someone into the blind state, even if only for a second.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成了动词：把人置于失明的状态，哪怕只有一秒钟。

intro.en: Blind is a thousand-year-old English word whose physical sense later grew a figurative one.
intro.cn: blind 是有一千多年历史的英语词，身体层面的义项后来长出了比喻用法。

items.en: Old English blind already meant unable to see, and it has kept that sense for a thousand years.
items.cn: 古英语 blind 已经表示看不见，这个义项保留了一千年。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family; German blind and Dutch blind carry the same meaning.
items.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语族，德语 blind 与荷兰语 blind 意思相同。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; some scholars link it to a root for confusion or darkness.
items.cn: 更早的来源并不确定，有学者把它与表示「混乱」或「黑暗」的词根联系起来。

items.en: Middle English writers used blind for rash judgement, and that figurative sense still lives.
items.cn: 中古英语作家用 blind 指草率的判断，这个比喻义至今仍在。

items.en: The slatted window covering took the name because it shuts out light, and the verb followed later.
items.cn: 板条窗饰因为挡光而得到这个名字，动词用法则出现得更晚。

intro.cn: blind 是基础形容词、名词兼动词，下面列出的是它的后缀以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin caecus and caecitas are recorded words for blind and blindness; they are parallels, not the source of blind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caecus 与 caecitas 分别是有记录的「瞎的」与「失明」，它们是平行词，不是 blind 的来源。

items.example: Blind is recorded in Old English.
items.exampleCN: blind 在古英语中已有记录。

definition_zh: 块；街区；大楼；堵塞；阻挡
definition_en: a solid piece of material, a group of buildings or a town square, or to stop something moving or happening
core_image: 一块方形水泥块把门口的路挡得死死的
scene: 工地门口，一块巨大的混凝土块挡住了整条小路。A huge block of concrete stood across the path.
sceneCN: 这里 block 是「块」（第 1 个义项：大块的固体材料）；句意为一块巨大的混凝土块横在路中间。

pos.zh: 名词：块；街区；大楼
动词：堵塞；阻挡

derivatives.zh: 由 block 加 -age 构成，义为「堵塞；阻塞物」
由 block 加 -er 构成，义为「阻挡者；封堵物」
由 block 加 -y 构成，义为「块状的；粗笨的」
由 block 与 buster 组合而成，义为「轰动一时的作品；大片」

senses.title: A solid piece
senses.definition: a large solid piece of wood, stone, concrete or similar material
senses.definitionCN: 木、石、混凝土等材料的大块固体
senses.example: He cut the meat into small blocks.
senses.exampleCN: 他把肉切成小块。
senses.why: The word first named a lump of wood or stone, and that solid piece is still the plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一块木头或石头，这个实心块状物仍是最朴素的义项。

senses.title: A town square
senses.definition: the area and buildings between two streets in a town, or the distance along it
senses.definitionCN: 城镇中两条街道之间的区域和建筑，也指这一段距离
senses.example: The bank is two blocks away.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在两个街区之外。
senses.why: American towns were laid out in square blocks, so one square of streets became a block.
senses.whyCN: 美国城镇按方形地块规划，于是一个方形街区就被称作 a block。

senses.title: A large building
senses.definition: a large building, especially one divided into flats or offices
senses.definitionCN: 大型建筑，尤指分成住宅单元或办公单元的楼
senses.example: They live in a block of flats.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在一栋公寓楼里。
senses.why: A big building looks like a solid block from the street, so British English calls it a block.
senses.whyCN: 大楼从街上看就像一整块实体，所以英式英语把它叫作 block。

senses.title: To clog a passage
senses.definition: to stop a pipe, drain or passage so that nothing can pass through
senses.definitionCN: 堵住管道、排水口或通道，使任何东西都无法通过
senses.example: Leaves blocked the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 树叶堵住了排水口。
senses.why: A block of material in a pipe stops the flow, so the noun turned into a verb of clogging.
senses.whyCN: 管道里的一块东西会阻断流动，于是这个名词变成了表示堵塞的动词。

senses.title: To stop from moving
senses.definition: to stop a person, vehicle, road or plan from moving forward or happening
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人、车辆、道路或计划前进或发生
senses.example: The police blocked the road.
senses.exampleCN: 警察封锁了道路。
senses.why: From blocking a physical path, the verb widened to blocking anything that should not get through.
senses.whyCN: 从挡住实体的路，这个动词扩展到阻挡任何不该通过的事物。

intro.en: Block came into English through French from Dutch, and it has moved from wood to streets to the act of stopping.
intro.cn: block 经法语从荷兰语进入英语，并从木头一路走到街区与「阻挡」的动作。

items.en: Middle English blok came from Old French bloc, meaning a lump or a wooden block.
items.cn: 中古英语 blok 来自古法语 bloc，意思是「块」或「木块」。

items.en: Old French took it from Middle Dutch blok, the word for a tree trunk cut short.
items.cn: 古法语又取自中古荷兰语 blok，指截短的树干。

items.en: Because blocks were used in building, the word spread to stone, concrete and brick pieces.
items.cn: 由于块材用于建筑，这个词扩展到石块、混凝土块和砖块。

items.en: American towns were laid out in squares, so a square of streets became a block.
items.cn: 美国城镇按方形地块规划，于是一个方形街区成了 a block。

items.en: From stopping a passage with a block, the verb grew the sense of blocking a road, a plan or a vote.
items.cn: 从用块状物堵住通道，动词长出了封锁道路、阻挡计划或否决投票的意思。

items.en: Today block covers a solid piece, a city square, one large building and the act of stopping.
items.cn: 今天 block 覆盖实心块、城市街区、大型建筑与阻挡动作。

note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收表示块状物与障碍的词。

entries.definition: Of the darkest colour, or without light.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「黑色的；黑暗的」，拼写与 block 相近。

entries.definition: To say that someone is responsible for something bad.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「责怪」，拼写与 block 相近。

entries.definition: Cold, empty and without hope.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒凉的；无望的」，拼写与 block 相近。

entries.definition: A hard rectangular block used for building walls.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「砖」，指砌墙用的硬质长方形块。

entries.definition: A thick, solid piece of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「厚块；大块」。

entries.definition: Something that stands in the way and stops progress.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「障碍」，指挡住前进的东西。

normal.cn: 块材用于建筑，所以这个词从木头扩展到石头与混凝土。

normal.en: American towns were laid out in squares, which is why a street square is a block.

normal.en: It commonly pairs with way, office, building and out.

abstract.en: See a square concrete block lying across a doorway: that is block.
abstract.cn: 想象一块方形混凝土块横在门口：那就是 block。

abstract.en: Walk around that block and you have gone one city block.
abstract.cn: 绕着那块地方走一圈，你就走过了一个街区。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the square stone bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那块方石把意思带回来。

root: block 经法语来自中古荷兰语 blok，原指截短的树干，后来扩展为木块、石块、混凝土块等实心块状物。因为块材用于建筑，它又指整栋大楼；美国城镇按方形地块规划，于是两条街之间的方形区域也叫 a block。由「用块状物堵住通道」，动词长出堵塞、阻挡与阻止的意思。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of block rest on one picture: a solid square that fills a space and stops what would otherwise pass.
sensesIntro.cn: block 的五个义项都立在同一个画面上：一个实心方块占住空间，挡住原本能通过的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square concrete block lying across a doorway
core.cn: 核心意象：一块方形混凝土块横在门口

branches.en: THE PIECE: the solid lump of wood or stone is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 块材线：木块或石块的实心体是最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE SQUARE: a planned square of streets became a town block.
branches.cn: 街区线：规划出的方形街道区域成了城市街区。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: a large building looks like one solid block.
branches.cn: 建筑线：大型建筑看上去就是一整块实体。

branches.en: THE CLOG: material in a pipe stops the flow and gives the verb its first sense.
branches.cn: 堵塞线：管道里的材料阻断流动，给出动词第一个义项。

branches.en: THE STOP: from a blocked path the verb widened to blocking anything.
branches.cn: 阻止线：从被挡住的路，这个动词扩展到阻挡任何事物。

definition_zh: 金发（的）；浅色的；金发女子
definition_en: having light yellow hair, or a person, especially a woman, with such hair
core_image: 阳光下的一头浅金色长发
scene: 照片里的姑娘站在海边，风吹起她浅金色的长发。The blonde girl stood by the sea with her hair in the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 blonde 是「金发的」（第 1 个义项：头发呈浅黄色的）；句意为那个金发女孩站在海边，头发随风飘起。

pos.zh: 形容词：金发的；浅色的
名词：金发女子；金发的人

derivatives.zh: 同一词的阳性或中性形式，义为「金发的」，美式英语中通用
由 blond 加 -ness 构成，义为「金发；浅色」
由 blond 加 -ish 构成，义为「略带金黄色的」

senses.title: Light yellow hair
senses.definition: having hair of a light yellow or pale golden colour
senses.definitionCN: 头发呈浅黄色或淡金色的
senses.example: She has long blonde hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她留着金色长发。
senses.why: The word came from French blond, and the -e ending still marks the feminine form in careful British use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自法语 blond，结尾的 -e 在讲究的英式用法里仍标记阴性形式。

senses.title: A person with such hair
senses.definition: a person, especially a woman, with light yellow hair
senses.definitionCN: 头发呈浅黄色的人，尤指女性
senses.example: The blonde walked into the room.
senses.exampleCN: 那位金发女子走进了房间。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun, so the hair colour can stand for the person who has it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词直接当名词用，于是发色可以代指拥有这种发色的人。

senses.title: A pale shade
senses.definition: used of wood, beer or other things that have a pale golden colour
senses.definitionCN: 用于木材、啤酒等呈淡金色的东西
senses.example: They ordered two glasses of blonde beer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们点了两杯浅色啤酒。
senses.why: The same pale golden colour appears in wood and beer, so the word stretched from hair to those materials.
senses.whyCN: 同样的淡金色也出现在木材和啤酒里，于是这个词从头发扩展到那些材料。

intro.en: Blonde came into English from French, and its spelling still carries a trace of French gender.
intro.cn: blonde 从法语进入英语，它的拼写仍带着法语性范畴的痕迹。

items.en: Old French blond meant light yellow, and it was used of hair and of pale gold.
items.cn: 古法语 blond 表示浅黄色，用于头发和淡金色。

items.en: The French word probably came from a medieval Latin form used for fair hair.
items.cn: 这个法语词可能来自中世纪拉丁语中描述浅色头发的形式。

items.en: English borrowed blonde in the seventeenth century, mostly to describe women's hair.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 blonde，主要用于描述女性的头发。

items.en: French marks feminine adjectives with -e, and English kept blonde for women and blond for men.
items.cn: 法语用 -e 标记阴性形容词，英语就把 blonde 留给女性，把 blond 留给男性。

items.en: American English now often uses blond for everyone, while British English still prefers blonde for women.
items.cn: 今天美式英语常用 blond 指所有人，英式英语仍偏好用 blonde 指女性。

entries.definition: The same word without the -e, used for men or for both sexes.

entries.definition: A flower, or the state of flowering.

entries.definition: Plain, dull and without much taste or interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「平淡的；乏味的」，拼写与 blonde 相近。

entries.definition: Light in colour, used of hair or skin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「浅色的」，可用于头发或皮肤。

entries.definition: Having the colour of gold.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「金色的」。

entries.definition: A woman with dark brown hair, the opposite of a blonde.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「深褐色头发的女子」，与金发女子相对。

definition_zh: 血；血液；血统；新鲜血液（新成员）
definition_en: the red liquid that flows through the body, family origin, or new members who bring fresh energy
core_image: 指尖划破后渗出的一滴红色液体
scene: 孩子摔倒擦破了膝盖，一滴血渗了出来。A drop of blood came from the cut on his knee.
sceneCN: 这里 blood 是「血」（第 1 个义项：在体内流动的红色液体）；句意为他的膝盖伤口渗出一滴血。

pos.zh: 名词：血；血液；血统；新成员
动词：使见血；让初次体验

derivatives.zh: 由 blood 加 -y 构成，义为「流血的；血腥的」
同族动词，义为「流血」
由 blood 加 -less 构成，义为「无血的；不流血的」
由 blood 与 stream 组合而成，义为「血流；血液循环」

senses.title: The red liquid
senses.definition: the red liquid that carries oxygen and food around the body
senses.definitionCN: 在体内运送氧气和养分的红色液体
senses.example: A drop of blood fell on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴血落在地板上。
senses.why: Old English blod named the red liquid itself, and this physical sense is still the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 blod 指的就是这种红色液体，这个身体层面的义项仍是词义的中心。

senses.title: Family origin
senses.definition: the family or national group a person comes from
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所属的家庭或民族群体
senses.example: She is of Italian blood.
senses.exampleCN: 她有意大利血统。
senses.why: Parents pass life to children through blood in old beliefs, so blood came to mean family origin.
senses.whyCN: 旧时认为父母通过血把生命传给孩子，于是 blood 引申为家族出身。

senses.title: New members
senses.definition: new people brought into a group to give it fresh energy
senses.definitionCN: 被引入某个群体、为其带来新活力的人
senses.example: The team needs new blood.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队需要新鲜血液。
senses.why: Fresh blood keeps a body alive, so new members are pictured as the blood a group needs.
senses.whyCN: 新鲜的血液让身体保持活力，所以新成员被比作一个群体所需要的血。

intro.en: Blood is an old English word with a Germanic family, and its figurative senses grew from the body to family and groups.
intro.cn: blood 是古老的英语词，属于日耳曼语族，它的比喻义从身体延伸到家族与群体。

items.en: Old English blod named the red liquid in the body and had the same shape as its Germanic relatives.

senses.title: To send out air
senses.definition: to send air out of the mouth, or to move air with force
senses.definitionCN: 把空气从口中送出，或用力量推动空气
senses.example: She blew on the hot soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她对着热汤吹气。
senses.why: Old English blawan meant to breathe out hard, and blowing out air is still the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 blawan 意为用力呼气，把空气吹出去仍是第一个义项。

senses.title: Of wind
senses.definition: used of the wind: to move strongly
senses.definitionCN: 用于风：强劲地移动
senses.example: The wind blew all night.
senses.exampleCN: 风刮了一整夜。
senses.why: The wind does the same thing a mouth does on a larger scale, so the verb serves both.
senses.whyCN: 风做的事和嘴做的事只是规模不同，所以同一个动词两处都管。

senses.title: To make a sound
senses.definition: to play a horn, whistle or other instrument by sending air through it
senses.definitionCN: 把空气送过号角、哨子或其他乐器来演奏
senses.example: He blew a whistle to stop the game.
senses.exampleCN: 他吹响哨子叫停了比赛。
senses.why: An instrument sounds when air is blown through it, so playing it is simply another blow.
senses.whyCN: 乐器因为空气被吹进去才发声，所以演奏不过是另一种「吹」。

senses.title: To burst apart
senses.definition: to break open or destroy something with an explosion
senses.definitionCN: 用爆炸使某物破裂或摧毁
senses.example: The storm blew down the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨把旧墙吹倒了。
senses.why: A blast of air or gas can tear a thing apart, so the word grew a sense of violent bursting.
senses.whyCN: 一股气体或气流能把东西撕裂，于是这个词长出了猛烈爆开的意思。

senses.title: A hard hit
senses.definition: a hard hit with the hand or a weapon, or a sudden bad event
senses.definitionCN: 用手或武器的一记重击，也指突如其来的坏事
senses.example: Losing the job was a heavy blow.
senses.exampleCN: 失去工作是沉重的打击。
senses.why: The noun first named a stroke or hit, and later any sharp misfortune that lands like one.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词最初指一记击打，后来泛指任何像一记重拳那样落下的不幸。

scene: 晴朗的午后，孩子抬头看着没有一丝云的天。The sky was deep blue above the child.

senses.title: The colour of the sky
senses.definition: the colour of a clear sky in daylight, between green and violet
senses.definitionCN: 白天晴空的颜色，介于绿色与紫色之间
senses.example: She painted the wall light blue.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成浅蓝色。
senses.why: Old French bleu gave English the colour word, and the sky has kept it as the everyday example.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 bleu 把颜色词带进英语，而天空一直是这个词最日常的例子。

senses.title: Sad and low
senses.definition: feeling sad, tired or without hope, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 感到悲伤、疲惫或没有希望，多用于口语
senses.example: He felt blue after the letter arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 收到那封信后他心情低落。
senses.why: Cold blue light and long dark evenings were linked to low spirits, so the colour became a word for sadness.
senses.whyCN: 冷蓝色的光与漫长昏暗的傍晚被联系到低落情绪，于是这个颜色词成了悲伤的说法。

senses.title: The music
senses.definition: a style of slow sad music that began among African American musicians
senses.definitionCN: 起源于非洲裔美国音乐人的缓慢忧伤的音乐风格
senses.example: The band played the blues all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队整晚都在演奏蓝调。
senses.why: The music took its name from the low mood it expresses, and it kept the plural form the blues.
senses.whyCN: 这种音乐因所表达的忧郁而得名，并保留了复数形式 the blues。

senses.title: Rude in content
senses.definition: dealing with sex in a rude or shocking way, used of jokes and films
senses.definitionCN: 以粗俗或令人震惊的方式涉及性，用于玩笑、影片等
senses.example: The film is too blue for young viewers.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影太粗俗，不适合年轻观众。
senses.why: Stage performers used blue as a coded word for material too bold for polite talk, and the sense stayed.
senses.whyCN: 旧时艺人用 blue 作为暗语，指不宜在雅言中提及的内容，这个义项保留至今。

intro.en: Blue came into English from French, and it has spread from the sky to moods, music and even rude jokes.
intro.cn: blue 从法语进入英语，并从天空一路扩展到情绪、音乐乃至粗俗的玩笑。

items.en: Old French bleu named the colour, and English borrowed it in the Middle English period.
items.cn: 古法语 bleu 表示这种颜色，英语在中古英语时期借入。

items.en: The French word goes back to a Germanic root that also gave the English word blow in an older sense of pale.
items.cn: 这个法语词可追溯到日耳曼语词根，同根词在古义中也有「浅色」的意思。

items.en: From the sixteenth century blue described a low, sad mood, perhaps from the look of cold winter light.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，blue 形容低落悲伤的情绪，可能源自寒冷冬日光线的观感。

items.en: African American musicians named their slow sad music the blues, and the phrase spread worldwide.
items.cn: 非洲裔美国音乐人把他们缓慢忧伤的音乐称作 the blues，这个说法传遍世界。

items.en: Today blue covers the colour, sadness, the music and, in older usage, rude material.
items.cn: 今天 blue 覆盖颜色、忧郁、这种音乐，以及在较老用法中的粗俗内容。

root: blue 来自古法语 bleu，英语在中古英语时期借入，其词根可追溯到日耳曼语，古义中有「浅色」之意。从十六世纪起，这个词因寒冷冬日光线与低落情绪的联系而表示「忧伤」。非洲裔美国音乐人把缓慢忧伤的音乐称作 the blues，这个说法传遍世界。较老的用法里，blue 还指不宜雅言的粗俗内容。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of blue grow from one picture: the deep colour of the sky, and then the moods and arts that colour came to stand for.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deep blue sky at noon without a cloud

branches.cn: 颜色线：天空给出 blue 最日常的颜色义项。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: the blues took its name from the low mood it sings.
branches.cn: 音乐线：the blues 因它所唱的忧郁而得名。

branches.en: THE BOLD TALK: stage slang made blue a coded word for rude material.
branches.cn: 粗俗线：舞台暗语让 blue 成为不宜雅言的内容的代称。

branches.en: THE SHADE: the colour and the mood share one picture of cold light.

scene: 木工房里，师傅把两块长木板并排钉在一起，做成一扇门。The carpenter nailed two boards together to make a door.

senses.title: A flat piece of wood
senses.definition: a long thin flat piece of wood or similar material used in building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑用的长而薄的平整木料或类似材料
senses.example: He nailed two boards together.
senses.exampleCN: 他把两块木板钉在一起。
senses.why: Old English bord meant a plank, and that flat piece of timber is still the plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bord 指一块木板，这种平整的木材仍是最朴素的义项。

senses.title: A governing group
senses.definition: a group of people who manage or direct a company or organization
senses.definitionCN: 管理或领导公司、机构的一组人
senses.example: The board approved the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会批准了新方案。

senses.title: To get on a vehicle

items.cn: 荷兰语 bord 与德语 Brett 是同源词，都指一块平整的木头。

sceneCN: 这里 body 是「身体」（第 1 个义项：人或动物的整个躯体）；句意为男孩在镜子里打量自己的身体。

pos.zh: 名词：身体；尸体；主体；团体
形容词：身体的（用于复合词）

derivatives.zh: 由 body 加 -ly 构成，义为「身体的；肉体的」
由 any 与 body 组合而成，义为「任何人」
由 every 与 body 组合而成，义为「每个人」
由 embody 加 -ment 构成，义为「体现；化身」

senses.title: The living frame
senses.definition: the whole physical structure of a person or animal, including flesh and bones
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物的整个躯体，包括血肉与骨骼
senses.example: Exercise keeps the body strong.
senses.exampleCN: 锻炼使身体强壮。
senses.why: Old English bodig meant the whole trunk and frame of a person, and that physical sense is still central.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bodig 指人的整个躯干与骨架，这个身体义项仍是中心。

senses.title: A dead person
senses.definition: the physical remains of a dead person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 死去的人或动物留下的躯体
senses.example: The police found the body in the river.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在河里发现了尸体。
senses.why: When life has gone, what remains is still the body, so the same word names a corpse.
senses.whyCN: 生命离去之后，剩下的仍然是身体，于是同一个词也指尸体。

senses.title: The main part
senses.definition: the main or central part of a thing, such as a document, car or building
senses.definitionCN: 事物最主要或居中的部分，如文件、汽车或建筑的主体
senses.example: The body of the report is twenty pages long.
senses.exampleCN: 报告正文有二十页。
senses.why: The main part holds everything else together the way a body holds limbs, so it is called the body.
senses.whyCN: 主体像身体承托四肢那样把其余部分撑住，所以它被称作 body。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: a group of people who act together, especially one with official power
senses.definitionCN: 共同行动的一群人，尤指拥有正式权力的机构
senses.example: A school body meets to discuss the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 学校的管理机构开会讨论新规定。
senses.why: A group is pictured as one body made of many members, so an organization is also a body.
senses.whyCN: 一群人被比作由许多成员组成的一个身体，所以组织也被称作 body。

senses.title: The shell of a vehicle
senses.definition: the main outer shell of a car, plane or ship
senses.definitionCN: 汽车、飞机或船只的主要外壳
senses.example: The body of the car was badly damaged.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车的车身严重受损。
senses.why: The shell of a vehicle surrounds its parts just as a body surrounds organs, so it takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 车体外壳像身体包裹器官那样包住各个部件，于是得到同一个名字。

intro.en: Body is an old English word for the whole frame of a living thing, and its image has been applied to objects and groups.
intro.cn: body 是古英语中表示生物整体躯干的词，它的意象被应用到物体与群体上。

items.en: Old English bodig meant the trunk and whole frame of a person or animal.
items.cn: 古英语 bodig 指人或动物的躯干与整个躯体。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic group, though the exact relatives differ from language to language.
items.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语族，但具体同源词在各语言中并不完全相同。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; some scholars suggest a root connected with swelling or growing.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定，有学者推测与表示「膨胀、生长」的词根有关。

items.en: English applied body to the main part of a document, a vehicle and a group of people.
items.cn: 英语把 body 用到文件主体、车体以及一群人身上。

items.en: Today body covers the living frame, a corpse, a main part and an organization.
items.cn: 今天 body 覆盖活着的躯体、尸体、主体与机构。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects words for flesh and groups.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收与躯体、群体有关的词。

entries.definition: The plural form of body.
entries.definitionCN: body 的复数形式，义为「多个身体」。

entries.definition: A close friend, used in informal speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伙伴；好友」，拼写与 body 相近。

entries.definition: Thin, with bones showing, or full of bones.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「瘦骨嶙峋的；多骨的」，读音与 body 接近。

entries.definition: A dead body, especially of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「尸体」，尤指人的遗体。

entries.definition: The main part of the body, without head or limbs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「躯干」，指不含头与四肢的身体主体。

entries.definition: A group with a purpose and a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「组织」，对应 body 的团体义。

normal.en: Old English bodig meant the trunk and whole frame of a living thing.
normal.cn: 古英语 bodig 指生物的整体躯干与骨架。

normal.en: When life is gone the frame remains, which is why a corpse is also a body.
normal.cn: 生命离去后骨架仍在，所以尸体也叫 body。

normal.en: A main part holds the rest together, so documents and cars have a body too.
normal.cn: 主体把其余部分撑住，所以文件和汽车也有 body。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with language, temperature, water and governing.
normal.cn: 它常与 language、temperature、water、governing 搭配。

normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-d-y，加复数词尾时 y 变成 i。

abstract.en: See a person turn before a mirror and look from head to feet: that whole frame is the body.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在镜前转身，从头看到脚：那一整副骨架就是 body。

abstract.en: Strip away the living parts of a car and its shell is still called a body.
abstract.cn: 把汽车的活动部件拿走，剩下的外壳仍被称作 body。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the mirror bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那面镜子把意思带回来。

examples.cn: 锻炼使身体强壮。

examples.en: The police found the body in the river.
examples.cn: 警方在河里发现了尸体。

examples.en: The body of the car was badly damaged.
examples.cn: 汽车的车身严重受损。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「巴迪」——镜子前从头到脚一整副：身体

root: body 来自古英语 bodig，指人或动物的躯干与整个躯体，属于日耳曼语族，但具体同源词在各语言中不完全一致；更早来源不确定，有学者推测与表示「膨胀、生长」的词根有关。英语把这个词扩展到文件主体、车体与一群人：主体像身体承托四肢，群体像由许多成员组成的一个身体。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of body rest on one picture: a whole frame that holds all its parts together, whether it is a person, a text, a car or a group.
sensesIntro.cn: body 的五个义项都立在同一个画面上：把各部分聚在一起的一整副骨架，无论它是人、文本、汽车还是一个群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person turning before a mirror and looking from head to feet
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在镜前转身，从头看到脚

branches.en: THE FRAME: the living structure of flesh and bone is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 躯体线：血肉与骨骼构成的活体是最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE REMAINS: when life leaves, the same frame is called a body still.
branches.cn: 遗体线：生命离开后，同一副骨架仍被称作 body。

branches.en: THE CENTRE: the main part of a text or thing holds the rest together.
branches.cn: 主体线：文本或事物的主要部分把其余部分撑住。

branches.en: THE GROUP: many members are pictured as one body.
branches.cn: 群体线：许多成员被比作一个身体。

branches.en: THE SHELL: a vehicle's outer shell surrounds its parts like a body.
branches.cn: 外壳线：车体外壳像身体那样包住各个部件。

definition_zh: 煮沸；沸腾；煮（食物）；（口语）发怒
definition_en: to heat a liquid until it bubbles, to cook food in boiling water, or to be very angry
core_image: 锅里翻腾的水和上升的白汽
scene: 厨房里，锅中的水开始翻滚，白色蒸汽升到窗上。The water in the pot began to boil.
sceneCN: 这里 boil 是「沸腾」（第 2 个义项：液体受热翻滚）；句意为锅里的水开始沸腾。

pos.zh: 动词：煮沸；沸腾；煮；（口语）发怒
名词：煮沸状态；沸点

derivatives.zh: 由 boil 加 -er 构成，义为「锅炉；热水器」
由 boil 加 -ing 构成，义为「沸腾的；极热的」
由 hard 与 boiled 组合而成，义为「煮得全熟的；硬心肠的」

senses.title: To heat a liquid
senses.definition: to heat a liquid until it reaches the temperature where it bubbles strongly
senses.definitionCN: 把液体加热到强烈冒泡的温度
senses.example: She boiled the water for tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她烧开水泡茶。
senses.why: Latin bulla meant a bubble, and boiling is exactly the moment when bubbles rise through a liquid.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 bulla 意为「气泡」，而沸腾正是气泡从液体里升起的时刻。

senses.title: To bubble with heat
senses.definition: used of a liquid: to bubble and turn to steam when heated
senses.definitionCN: 用于液体：受热时冒泡并变成蒸汽
senses.example: The soup is boiling on the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 汤在炉子上沸腾。
senses.why: The same event is seen from the liquid's side, so the verb also works without an object.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事也可以从液体这一边看，所以这个动词也能不带宾语。

senses.title: To cook in water
senses.definition: to cook food by keeping it in water that is boiling
senses.definitionCN: 把食物放在沸腾的水中煮熟
senses.example: He boiled two eggs for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 他煮了两个鸡蛋当早餐。
senses.why: Boiling water is the oldest cooking tool, so the verb moved from the water to the food in it.
senses.whyCN: 沸水是最古老的烹饪工具，于是这个动词从水移到水里的食物。

senses.title: To be furious
senses.definition: to be extremely angry, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 极度愤怒，多用于口语
senses.example: He was boiling when he heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息时他怒不可遏。
senses.why: Anger is felt as heat rising inside, so boiling became a picture of furious emotion.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被感受为体内升起的热，于是「沸腾」成了暴怒的画面。

intro.en: Boil goes back through French to Latin words for a bubble, and the bubble is still visible in its meaning.
intro.cn: boil 经法语可追溯到拉丁语中表示「气泡」的词，气泡至今仍留在它的词义里。

items.en: Latin bulla meant a bubble or a round object, the picture behind the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bulla 意为气泡或圆形物，这是整个词族的画面来源。

items.en: The verb bullire meant to bubble, and it described liquid rising in round bursts.
items.cn: 动词 bullire 意为冒泡，描述液体成团上涌的样子。

items.en: Old French turned the Latin verb into boillir, still meaning to boil or bubble.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁动词变成 boillir，仍表示煮沸或冒泡。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the verb as boilen, first for liquid and then for cooking.
items.cn: 中古英语借入动词 boilen，先用于液体，后用于烹饪。

items.en: Today boil covers heating liquid, bubbling, cooking and, informally, furious anger.
items.cn: 今天 boil 覆盖加热液体、冒泡、烹饪以及口语中的暴怒。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects other cooking and heat words.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收其他烹饪与加热的词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「锅炉；热水器」，由 boil 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A thick liquid used for cooking or machines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「油」，读音与 boil 接近。

entries.definition: A length of wire wound into rings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「线圈」，读音与 boil 接近。

entries.definition: To cook slowly just below the boiling point.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「小火慢煮」，温度略低于沸点。

entries.definition: To cook food with the hot vapour of boiling water.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「蒸」，用沸水产生的热蒸汽烹饪。

entries.definition: A ball of air or gas in a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气泡」，正是 boil 词源里的那个画面。

normal.en: Old French boillir and Middle English boilen carry the same meaning forward.

normal.en: It commonly pairs with water, egg, point and over.

normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-i-l，中间的 oi 读得像 coin 里的音。

abstract.cn: 想象气泡从锅里升起，白色蒸汽爬到窗上：那就是 boil。

abstract.en: Let the same heat rise inside a person and the word becomes anger.
abstract.cn: 让同样的热在一个人体内升起，这个词就变成了愤怒。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the rising bubbles bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那些上升的气泡把意思带回来。

root: boil 经古法语 boillir 追溯到拉丁语 bullire（冒泡），而 bullire 又来自 bulla（气泡）。中古英语借入作 boilen，先用于液体受热翻滚，再用于把食物放在沸水里煮。现代英语里，这个动词还用来表示体内热感升腾的暴怒。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of boil rest on one picture: heat making bubbles rise, whether in a pot, in food, or inside an angry person.
sensesIntro.cn: boil 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：热让气泡升起，无论在锅里、在食物里，还是在愤怒的人体内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bubbles climbing through a pot while steam rises
core.cn: 核心意象：气泡从锅里升起，蒸汽同时上腾

branches.en: THE HEAT: heating a liquid until it bubbles is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 加热线：把液体加热到冒泡是最朴素的义项。

branches.en: THE BUBBLES: the liquid's own bubbling is the same event seen from inside.
branches.cn: 气泡线：液体自身的翻滚是同一事件从内部看到的样子。

branches.en: THE POT: boiling water became the oldest way to cook food.
branches.cn: 锅线：沸水成了最古老的烹饪方式。

branches.en: THE TEMPER: rising heat inside a person pictures furious anger.
branches.cn: 脾气线：体内升起的热，比喻暴怒。

branches.en: THE STATE: heating and bubbling are two views of one moment.
branches.cn: 状态线：加热与冒泡是同一时刻的两种视角。

definition_zh: 书；书本；本子；账簿；预订
definition_en: a set of printed pages held together, a record book, or to arrange for something in advance
core_image: 桌上摊开的一本书，书页微微翘起
scene: 傍晚的书桌上，一本摊开的书被台灯照亮，书页还压着一支笔。An open book lay on the desk under the lamp.
sceneCN: 这里 book 是「书」（第 1 个义项：装订成册的读物）；句意为台灯下书桌上摊着一本书。

pos.zh: 名词：书；书本；本子；账簿
动词：预订；登记

derivatives.zh: 由 book 加 -ing 构成，义为「预订；预约」
由 book 加 -let 构成，义为「小册子」
由 book 与 shop 组合而成，义为「书店」
由 book 与 mark 组合而成，义为「书签」

senses.title: A bound set of pages
senses.definition: a set of printed or written pages bound together in a cover
senses.definitionCN: 装订在封面内的一册印刷或书写页面
senses.example: She read a book on the train.
senses.exampleCN: 她在火车上读了一本书。
senses.why: Old English boc named a written document, and the bound pages of a book are its clearest modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 boc 指书写文献，装订成册的书页是它今天最清楚的义项。

senses.title: A blank or ruled notebook
senses.definition: a blank or ruled set of pages used for writing notes
senses.definitionCN: 用于记笔记的空白或带格线的册子
senses.example: He wrote the address in his book.
senses.exampleCN: 他把地址写在自己的本子上。
senses.why: Before printing, any set of pages for writing was a book, and exercise books keep that sense.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷术之前，任何用于书写的页册都叫 book，练习本保留了这个义项。

senses.title: A record of accounts
senses.definition: a record of money, names or events kept by a business or group
senses.definitionCN: 企业或团体保存的钱款、名单或事件记录
senses.example: The clerk checked the books at closing time.
senses.exampleCN: 店员在打烊时核对了账簿。
senses.why: Accounts were written into bound books, so the books themselves became the name of the records.
senses.whyCN: 账目写在装订的册子里，于是这些册子本身成了记录的代称。

senses.title: To arrange in advance
senses.definition: to arrange for a room, seat, ticket or service to be kept for you
senses.definitionCN: 事先安排，让别人为你留出房间、座位、票或服务
senses.example: I booked a room for two nights.
senses.exampleCN: 我订了房间住两晚。
senses.why: A booking was first written into a book of records, so reserving something took the name of the book.
senses.whyCN: 预订最初要写进一本记录册，于是「预留」这件事就借用了 book 这个名字。

intro.en: Book is an old word for a written document, and it may be linked to the beech tree whose wood carried early writing.
intro.cn: book 是表示书写文献的古词，它可能与山毛榉有关，因为早期文字刻在这种木头上。

items.en: Old English boc meant a written document or a charter, not yet the bound volume of today.
items.cn: 古英语 boc 指书写文献或契据，还不是今天装订成册的书。

items.en: The word is related to beech, because early letters were cut into smooth beech boards.

definition_zh: 使厌烦；钻孔；令人厌烦的人；口径
definition_en: to make someone feel tired and uninterested, to make a hole, or the width of a gun barrel
core_image: 钻头一点点钻进木板，木屑顺着螺旋退出
scene: 木工把钻头对准木板，机器转动，一个圆孔慢慢钻了出来。The drill bored a neat hole in the wood.

senses.title: To make someone tired
senses.definition: to make someone feel tired and uninterested because something is dull
senses.definitionCN: 因为事情乏味而让人感到疲倦、提不起兴趣
senses.example: The long talk bored the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 那场冗长的讲话让全班都很厌烦。
senses.why: The dull sense grew in the eighteenth century from the idea of wearing a person down, like a drill wearing through wood.
senses.whyCN: 「乏味」这个义项在十八世纪出现，来自把人一点点磨下去的意思，像钻头磨穿木头。

senses.title: To make a hole
senses.definition: to make a round hole in something with a drill or similar tool
senses.definitionCN: 用钻具或类似工具在某物上打出圆孔
senses.example: They bored a hole in the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在墙上钻了一个孔。
senses.why: Old English borian meant to pierce, and making a hole is the oldest sense of this word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 borian 意为刺穿，打孔是这个词最古老的义项。

senses.title: A dull person
senses.definition: a person or thing that makes others feel tired and uninterested
senses.definitionCN: 让别人感到疲倦、提不起兴趣的人或事物
senses.example: He is a bore at every party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在每个聚会上都是个乏味的人。
senses.why: The verb became a noun, so the person who bores others is simply called a bore.
senses.whyCN: 动词变成名词，于是让别人厌烦的人就直接被叫作 a bore。

senses.title: The width of a barrel
senses.definition: the inside width of a gun barrel or of a tube
senses.definitionCN: 枪管或管子的内部直径
senses.example: The gun has a narrow bore.
senses.exampleCN: 这把枪的口径很窄。
senses.why: The width of a barrel is the width of the hole bored through it, so bore also names that measure.
senses.whyCN: 枪管的宽度就是钻穿它的孔的宽度，所以 bore 也指这个尺寸。

items.en: The verb then produced the noun bore for a dull person or task.

core_image: 产房里第一声啼哭
scene: 产房里传来一声响亮的啼哭，护士把裹好的婴儿抱到母亲身边。The baby was born just after midnight.

senses.title: Brought into life
senses.definition: brought into life when a baby comes out of its mother's body
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿从母体中出来、开始生命时
senses.example: She was born in a small village.
senses.exampleCN: 她出生在一个小村庄。
senses.why: Born is the old past participle of bear, meaning carried, so it first pictures a child carried into the world.
senses.whyCN: born 是 bear（承载）的古老过去分词，最初描画的是一个孩子被带到世上。

senses.title: Natural from the start
senses.definition: having a quality from birth rather than learning it
senses.definitionCN: 从出生起就具备某种特质，而非后天学来
senses.example: He is a born teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个天生的老师。
senses.why: If a quality is present at birth, it seems to come with the person, so born came to mean natural.
senses.whyCN: 一种特质若在出生时就有，看上去就是随人而来的，于是 born 引申为「天生的」。

senses.title: Beginning to exist
senses.definition: used of an idea, group or situation that starts to exist
senses.definitionCN: 用于开始出现的想法、群体或局面
senses.example: The idea was born in a late-night talk.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法诞生于一次深夜长谈。
senses.why: New ideas are pictured as newborns: they appear at a moment, small and needing care.
senses.whyCN: 新想法被比作新生儿：在某一刻出现，幼小且需要照料。

root: born 是古英语 boren，即动词 beran（承载、生育）的过去分词；德语 gebären 与荷兰语 baren 同属一个表示生育的词族。英语把两个过去分词分了工：born 用于出生，borne 用于承载其他事物。由「被带到世上」的画面，born 又引申为「天生的」，以及想法、群体、运动的「产生」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of born rest on one picture: a child carried into the world, and then anything that appears at a starting moment.
sensesIntro.cn: born 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：一个被带到世上的孩子，以及任何在一个开端时刻出现的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first cry in a delivery room
core.cn: 核心意象：产房里的第一声啼哭

branches.en: THE BIRTH: coming out of the mother's body is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 出生线：从母体中出来是最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE NATURE: a quality present at birth is called born.
branches.cn: 天性线：出生时就有的特质被称作 born。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: ideas and groups are pictured as newborns too.
branches.cn: 起源线：想法与群体也被比作新生儿。

branches.en: THE START: birth and inborn quality share the same beginning.
branches.cn: 开端线：出生与天生的特质共享同一个开端。

branches.en: THE APPEARING: a baby and a new idea both come into being.
branches.cn: 出现线：婴儿与新想法都是「开始存在」。

intro.en: Born is a past participle used as an adjective, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: born 是作形容词用的过去分词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin natus and nasci are recorded words for born and to be born; they are parallels, not the source of born.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 natus 与 nasci 分别是有记录的「出生的」与「出生」，它们是平行词，不是 born 的来源。

items.example: Boren is the recorded Old English form.
items.exampleCN: boren 是有记录的古英语形式。

definition_zh: 借入；借用；借钱；借用（词语、想法）
definition_en: to take something from someone with the intention of giving it back
core_image: 从朋友手里接过一本书，答应下周归还
scene: 图书馆的柜台前，学生把借书卡递过去，接过一本厚重的词典。She borrowed a dictionary from the library.
sceneCN: 这里 borrow 是「借入」（第 1 个义项：拿走某物并打算归还）；句意为她从图书馆借了一本词典。

pos.zh: 动词：借入；借用；借钱

derivatives.zh: 由 borrow 加 -er 构成，义为「借用者；借款人」
由 borrow 加 -ing 构成，义为「借入；借款」
由 borrowing 加 -s 构成，义为「借词」，指从其他语言借入的词

senses.title: To take and return
senses.definition: to take something from someone and agree to give it back later
senses.definitionCN: 从别人那里拿走某物，并约定以后归还
senses.example: Can I borrow your pen for a moment?
senses.exampleCN: 我能借你的笔用一下吗？
senses.why: Old English borgian meant to take on pledge, and a borrowed thing is held on the promise to return it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 borgian 意为以担保方式取得，借来的东西是在归还的许诺下持有的。

senses.title: To take money on loan
senses.definition: to take money from a person or bank and agree to pay it back
senses.definitionCN: 从个人或银行取得钱款，并约定偿还
senses.example: They borrowed money to buy the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们借钱买了房子。
senses.why: Money borrowing is the same promise in a heavier form: the pledge now includes interest.
senses.whyCN: 借钱是同一个许诺在更重的形式下的版本：担保里如今还包括利息。

senses.title: To take words or ideas
senses.definition: to take a word, idea or custom from another language or group
senses.definitionCN: 从另一种语言或群体取用词语、想法或习俗
senses.example: English borrowed many words from French.
senses.exampleCN: 英语从法语借用了许多词。
senses.why: A borrowed word is taken into a new language and, in a sense, never given back, which is why languages borrow too.
senses.whyCN: 借词被取进另一种语言，某种意义上再也不归还，所以语言之间也会「借」。

intro.en: Borrow comes from an old word for a pledge, and the promise to return is still inside it.
intro.cn: borrow 来自表示「担保」的古词，归还的许诺至今仍在这个词里。

items.en: Old English borgian meant to borrow or to lend, both resting on a pledge between two people.
items.cn: 古英语 borgian 既表示借入也表示借出，两者都建立在两人之间的担保上。

items.en: The noun borg meant a pledge or security, the thing that made a loan safe.
items.cn: 名词 borg 意为担保或抵押，是让借贷变得安全的凭据。

items.en: German borgen and Dutch borgen are relatives, both covering borrowing and lending.
items.cn: 德语 borgen 与荷兰语 borgen 是同源词，都兼指借入与借出。

items.en: The word was applied to languages, so a word taken from another tongue is a borrowing.
items.cn: 这个词也被用到语言上，于是从别的语言取来的词就叫借词。

items.en: Today borrow covers objects, money and words or ideas taken from others.
items.cn: 今天 borrow 覆盖物品、钱款以及取用他人的词语或想法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects words about lending and taking.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收与借贷、取用有关的词。

entries.definition: A hole dug in the ground by an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「地洞」，拼写与 borrow 相近。

entries.definition: Not wide, only a short distance across.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「狭窄的」，读音与 borrow 接近。

entries.definition: The past form of borrow, meaning taken and to be returned.
entries.definitionCN: borrow 的过去式，义为「借来的」。

entries.definition: To give something to someone for a time, expecting it back.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「借出」，与 borrow 方向相反。

entries.definition: Money lent, or to lend something for a time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「贷款；借出」。

entries.definition: To take a word, idea or method from elsewhere and use it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「采用」，对应 borrow 的借用词语义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English borgian rested on borg, a pledge, and a loan is still a promise.
normal.cn: 古英语 borgian 建立在 borg（担保）之上，而借贷至今仍是一个许诺。

normal.en: German borgen and Dutch borgen are relatives that cover borrowing and lending.
normal.cn: 德语 borgen 与荷兰语 borgen 是同源词，兼指借入与借出。

normal.en: A word taken from another language is called a borrowing because it never goes back.
normal.cn: 从另一种语言取来的词叫借词，因为它再也不会归还。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with from, money, book and idea.
normal.cn: 它常与 from、money、book、idea 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-o-r-r-o-w; the double r keeps the vowel short.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-r-r-o-w，双写的 r 让元音保持短促。

abstract.en: See a hand take a book and promise to bring it back next week: that is borrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手接过一本书，答应下周归还：那就是 borrow。

abstract.en: Stretch the same promise to money or to a word, and the word still fits.
abstract.cn: 把同一个许诺延伸到钱或一个词，这个词仍然适用。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the returned book bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那本归还的书把意思带回来。

examples.cn: 我能借你的笔用一下吗？

root: borrow 来自古英语 borgian，意为借入或借出，其名词 borg 意为担保或抵押，借贷至今仍是一种归还的许诺；德语 borgen 与荷兰语 borgen 是同源词。这个词后来也被用到语言上，从别的语言取来的词就叫 borrowing（借词）。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of borrow rest on one picture: taking something for a time under a promise to give it back.
sensesIntro.cn: borrow 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：在一段期限内拿走某物，并许诺归还。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand taking a book and promising to return it
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手接过一本书，答应归还

branches.en: THE OBJECT: taking a thing for a time is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 物品线：暂时取走一件东西是最朴素的义项。

branches.en: THE MONEY: the same promise grows heavier when interest is added.
branches.cn: 钱款线：加上利息之后，同一个许诺变得更重。

branches.en: THE WORD: languages take words from each other and never give them back.
branches.cn: 词语线：语言互相取用词语，而且从不归还。

branches.en: THE LOAN: objects and money share one pledge to return.
branches.cn: 借贷线：物品与钱款共享同一个归还的担保。

branches.en: THE TAKING: a thing and a word are both taken from elsewhere.
branches.cn: 取用线：物品与词语都是从别处取来的。
